chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakūnī, he said: ʿAlī عليه السلام said:
"Whoever has intercourse with a woman once, then is taken away from her, then she has no option."

key_terms.أَتَى: had intercourse with; approached sexually in this legal context
key_terms.أُخِّذَ: was taken away; here indicating separation or loss of access
key_terms.السَّكُونِيِّ: al-Sakūnī, the narrator through whom this report is transmitted
key_terms.امْرَأَةً: a woman; here meaning the wife in question
key_terms.خِيَارَ: legal option or right of choice to annul or separate

ai.seo_question: Does a wife retain the option of annulment if her husband had intercourse with her once and then became unable to do so?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning marital separation in the case discussed in the chapter on the impotent husband. It indicates that if intercourse occurred even once, the woman's option of annulment on that basis no longer remains.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4896 - In the narration of Al-Sakooni, it is reported that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"Whoever engages in intercourse with a woman even once and then is separated from her, she has no option (of annulment or separation) thereafter."
